name: bpmsoft-toolkit
description: Autocomplete, navigation, localization and naming tools for BPMSoft AMD modules in Pkg

commands.title: Пометить как ложное срабатывание (игнорировать это имя во всех проверках нейминга)
Local History: найти запись для восстановления…

bpmsoft.pkgGlob.description: Glob for package schema JS files to index

bpmsoft.platformUiGlob.description: Glob for platform Ext UI classes (override/extend targets like BPMSoft.controls.Grid)

bpmsoft.enablePlatformStubs.description: Include static BPMSoft.* platform stubs in completions

bpmsoft.preferIndexedCompletions.description: Disable JS word/name history suggestions in workspace so indexed BPMSoft completions rank first

bpmsoft.enumInlayHints.description: Show inline hints decoding coded numeric fields (dataValueType, itemType, contentType, comparisonType, business-rule ruleType/property) to their BPMSoft.* constant, and a short description at each rules/businessRules rule

bpmsoft.styleDiagnostics.description: Check style in editable JS and C# files. JS skips Autogenerated / UI / conf. C# also checks Autogenerated/Src (opened by C# Dev Kit). JS: K&R, var/const, eqeqeq, unused locals and schema members, switch, curly braces, camelCase methods/locals. C#: Allman braces, if/switch, naming conventions.

bpmsoft.csharpXmlDocDiagnostics.description: Warn when a public/protected C# method or property has no /// XML-doc comment above it. Off by default: existing codebases rarely have full XML-doc coverage, so this would be noisy until you opt in.

bpmsoft.trailingCommentDiagnostics.description: Warn when a // comment (JS or C#) sits at the end of a code line instead of on its own line above, per the JS/C# style guides. Disable if this is too noisy on an existing codebase that hasn't followed the convention.

bpmsoft.selectAllColumnsHint.description: Info-level hint on AddAllSchemaColumns()/FetchFromDB() without an explicit column list (C#) and esq.allColumns = true (JS): double-check you actually need every column. Silence a specific call site with a // bpmsoft-ignore: select-all-columns comment on the line above, or use the 'Not a problem' quick fix.

bpmsoft.formatting.enabled.description: Register BPMSoft's Format Document providers for JS/C#/SQL-script files (Prettier + our own style fixes for JS; brace/spacing/blank-line auto-fixes for C#; sql-formatter for Pkg/*/SqlScripts/*.sql). Works with the standard Format Document command / Shift+Alt+F / editor.formatOnSave. Turn off if you'd rather use another formatter for these languages.

bpmsoft.namingDiagnostics.description: Check client schema / C# schema / SQL script names against naming-guidelines.md §3/§4 (type-appropriate suffix — Section/SectionV2, Page/PageV2/MiniPage/ModalPage, Detail/DetailV2 — only enforced when the schema's own immediate parent is itself part of that family, e.g. BasePageV2/BaseSectionV2/BaseGridDetailV2; a rootless/unrelated-parent view model is exempt; for Module-type schemas, the module's own registered define()/Ext.define() name must match the schema Code, and a structurally-CSS module (empty .js, real .less) must be suffixed exactly Css; a wizard-injected numeric tail and New/Test/Temp/Copy in the business name are flagged too; and — only where the platform gives an unambiguous marker — Service/EventListener for C#). Surfaced both as squiggles on open descriptor.json/.js/.cs files and in the 'BPMSoft: Naming Issues' view.

bpmsoft.namingPrefixes.description: Comma-separated package/schema name prefixes to require (e.g. "Nau" or "Nau,Go" for multiple streams). Empty (default) disables the prefix check — there's no one universal prefix to assume.

bpmsoft.gitFlowDiagnostics.description: Check the current git branch against the team's Git Flow model (main/develop/sprint/x.x.x/release/x.x.x/feature/bugfix) and show violations in the status bar. Covers: branch name pattern, main never carrying commits absent from develop, and (see bpmsoft.gitFlow.checkBranchParent) feature/bugfix branched from the right parent. Can't check step *order* — that's not recoverable from git history alone.

bpmsoft.gitFlow.checkBranchParent.description: Heuristically check that feature/* was branched from a sprint/* branch and bugfix/* from a release/* branch, not straight off develop/main — based on merge-base analysis of git history, so it can false-positive on a branch that was created correctly but never rebased/updated from its parent. Turn off if it's too noisy; the other bpmsoft.gitFlowDiagnostics checks are unaffected.

bpmsoft.packageOwnershipDiagnostics.description: Check the active file's package against bpmsoft.namingPrefixes and bpmsoft.expectedMaintainers (stand-ins for the SchemaNamePrefix/Maintainer system settings — no DB connection to read those directly), reading each package's own descriptor.json. Violations show in the status bar.

bpmsoft.currentPackage.description: Reference value for the package you're currently working in — stand-in for the CurrentPackageId system setting. Shown in the 'Package Settings' view; not yet enforced as a check (see bpmsoft.packageOwnershipDiagnostics for what actually is).

bpmsoft.expectedMaintainers.description: Comma-separated Maintainer value(s) your team's packages should have (e.g. "YandexGo") — stand-in for the Maintainer system setting. Empty (default) disables the maintainer check.

bpmsoft.entityNamingDiagnostics.description: Check EntitySchemaManager objects (naming-guidelines.md §2 'Объекты') against their own descriptor.json/metadata.json/Resources: object Code (PascalCase, prefix, singular, no Tbl/Entity/Field affix), ru-RU/en-US Title coverage, custom column Code (prefix, boolean Is/Has/Can prefix, date suffix, no redundant lookup 'Id' suffix, no redundant repetition of the owning entity's name), and cross-package Code uniqueness (aware of the substitution mechanism — the same Code across packages via ExtendParent is expected, not a collision).

bpmsoft.entityNaming.checkSingularName.description: Part of bpmsoft.entityNamingDiagnostics: flag an object Code that looks plural. Kept as its own toggle — English has no reliable syntactic plural rule without a dictionary, so this heuristic (ends in 's', not 'ss'/'us'/'is') is noisier than the other checks.

bpmsoft.entityNaming.singularExceptions.description: Comma-separated object Codes that are legitimately plural by meaning, exempt from bpmsoft.entityNaming.checkSingularName.

bpmsoft.entityNaming.dateSuffixes.description: Comma-separated acceptable suffixes for DATE/DATE_TIME/TIME column names (e.g. CreatedOn/ModifiedOn → "On", StartDate → "Date").

bpmsoft.entityNaming.booleanPrefixes.description: Comma-separated acceptable verb/assertion prefixes for BOOLEAN column names (e.g. IsActive, HasAttachment, CanEdit).

bpmsoft.sqlTempScriptMaxAgeDays.description: naming-guidelines.md §6: a _Temp SQL script should be removed from the package after its one-time run on target environments. This extension can't know what's actually been deployed, so it's a nudge, not a hard check — a _Temp script older than this many days (by its git add date) gets flagged as 'possibly forgotten'. 0 disables it.

bpmsoft.processNamingDiagnostics.description: Check ProcessSchemaManager business processes (naming-guidelines.md §7 'Бизнес-процессы') against their own descriptor.json/metadata.json/Resources: process Code (PascalCase, prefix, mandatory 'Process' suffix, no temporary designation like New/Test/Temp/Copy/V2), ru-RU/en-US Title coverage, and per-diagram-element title rules — Actions should start with a verb, Events should describe an already-happened fact (past tense), Exclusive gateways are recommended as closed questions, and a Sequence flow without a transition condition should normally be left unnamed. The Action/Event checks are weak word-ending heuristics (no real Russian morphology available) and can be noisy — same trade-off as the SQL script pattern check.

bpmsoft.processUserTaskNamingDiagnostics.description: Check ProcessUserTaskSchemaManager schemas (naming-guidelines.md §8 'Действие процесса (UserTask)') against their own descriptor.json/metadata.json/Resources: UserTask Code (PascalCase, prefix, mandatory 'UserTask' suffix, business name starting with a verb from bpmsoft.processUserTask.actionVerbs), ru-RU/en-US Title coverage, and parameter Code (no Tbl/Entity/Field technical affix). The Input/Output parameter-direction-suffix recommendation is a separate opt-in, see bpmsoft.processUserTask.checkParameterDirectionSuffix.

bpmsoft.processUserTask.actionVerbs.description: Comma-separated whitelist of verbs a UserTask's own code (after the team prefix) is expected to start with (e.g. GoChangeDataUserTask → "Change"). A curated list rather than a heuristic — English has no reliable ending marker for 'this is a verb' the way Russian infinitives do.

bpmsoft.processUserTask.checkParameterDi.description: naming-guidelines.md §8: recommends an Input/Output suffix on parameter names when a UserTask has more than one, to indicate direction. Off by default — confirmed 0% real adoption across two installs (176 real parameters, none suffixed), so enabling this flags nearly every existing multi-parameter UserTask. Turn on if your team wants to start enforcing it going forward.

bpmsoft.dataNamingDiagnostics.description: Check Data package items (naming-guidelines.md §5 'Данные') against their own descriptor.json/data.json: Code (PascalCase, must start with its target table's own name — Descriptor.Schema.Name, e.g. Lookup_X/City_Main/SysSettings_X all reduce to the same {TableName}_... template), no raw GUID/hash segment in the code, and — the platform-risk check — every SysSettings data schema must have a matching SysSettingsValue and vice versa, matched by the real seeded row Id/foreign key, not by folder name. A SysSettings without a SysSettingsValue can 400 when read; the reverse can be a legitimate override of a stock setting's value, so is worded as a hint rather than a hard violation.

bpmsoft.csharpNamingDiagnostics.description: Check C# schema code (naming-guidelines.md §4 'Исходный код') against every .cs file under Schemas/ — not just SourceCodeSchemaManager schemas, matching the guideline's own 'and similar server-side artifacts' scope: the package prefix, Service/EventListener suffix (only checked when the class actually inherits BaseService/BaseEntityEventListener or carries [ServiceContract]/[EntityEventListener] — no reliable platform marker exists for Helper/Manager/Handler/Repository/Client/Job, so those roles' suffixes aren't verified the same way, see bpmsoft.csharpNaming.checkRoleSuffix for the heuristic opt-in instead), the schema's registered name matching an actual class in the file, no redundant 'SourceCode' suffix, no temporary designation (New/Test/Temp/Copy/V2), and no chained/mixed role suffixes (e.g. ...ServiceHelper). ru-RU/en-US Title coverage is checked separately, only for real SourceCodeSchemaManager schemas (a Process/UserTask/Entity's own .cs file already has its Title checked by that schema type's own check).

bpmsoft.csharpNaming.checkRoleSuffix.description: Flag a C# schema Code that doesn't end in any of bpmsoft.csharpNaming.roleSuffixes at all (Helper/Manager/Handler/Repository/Client/Connector/Job/... have no base-class or interface marker to verify the suffix is actually correct, unlike Service/EventListener — this only checks that *some* recognized role suffix is present). Off by default — confirmed ~37-45% of real Source Code schemas across two installs end in none of the defaults, and a good share of those are legitimately something the guideline's table doesn't cover at all (Constants/DTO/Exception/Extensions/Callout classes, ...), not a missed suffix. Tune bpmsoft.csharpNaming.roleSuffixes to your own real patterns before turning this on.

bpmsoft.csharpNaming.roleSuffixes.description: Comma-separated role suffixes recognized as 'has a role suffix' (bpmsoft.csharpNaming.checkRoleSuffix) and checked for chaining/mixing (e.g. ...ServiceHelper, always on).

bpmsoft.csharpNaming.checkSingleClassPer.description: Flag a C# schema file that declares more than one top-level class. Off by default — naming-guidelines.md's own 'один основной класс — одна схема' rule has an explicit exception for a data object model, and ~26-27% of real Source Code schemas across two installs are legitimately multi-class (request/response DTOs alongside the main class) — this can't be told apart from a genuinely crammed-together schema automatically, so it's a team preference to opt into, not a default-on check.

bpmsoft.clientSchemaNaming.checkModuleSu.description: Flag a Module-type client schema (SchemaType: Module, not already recognized as Mixin/Css) whose Code doesn't end in Module or Mixin. Off by default — confirmed 74-84% of real Module-type schemas across two installs legitimately use neither (Helper/Constants/Container/Override/Design/...), the same open-role-vocabulary situation as bpmsoft.csharpNaming.checkRoleSuffix.

bpmsoft.naming.ignoredNames.description: Schema/process/data/class names excluded from every naming-guidelines.md check (client schema, Process, UserTask, Data, C#, SQL, Entity) — for a confirmed false positive that's structurally correct but doesn't fit this particular real name (e.g. 'Old' used as a legitimate business qualifier, not a stale-code marker). Set via the 'Пометить как ложное срабатывание' action on a naming finding (Naming Issues tree, or the quick fix on the squiggly), or edited directly.
